title_clean: The Many Kinds of Elements — Dependent Origination (MN 115)
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores dependent origination through the Bahudhātuka Sutta, examining causality and the first links of paṭicca samuppāda.
description_long:
In this teaching on the Bahudhātuka Sutta (MN 115), Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Buddha's foundational understanding of dependent origination (paṭicca samuppāda) and causality. He explores the famous formula 'when this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises' as the platform for understanding how phenomena arise through both linear causality from the past and present-moment conditions.

The talk focuses on the first crucial links of dependent origination: how ignorance (avijjā) — understood as fundamental not-knowing rather than culpable ignorance — conditions formations (saṅkhāra), which are our mental, verbal, and physical habits. These formations then condition consciousness (viññāṇa), which provides the screen upon which mentality-materiality (nāma-rūpa) and the six sense bases manifest, leading to contact (phassa).

Bhante emphasizes that this process occurs moment by moment, with underlying delusion creating habits that manifest on consciousness alongside our psychophysical organism. He explains how this understanding provides a middle way between fatalism and chaos, showing how karma operates through the interplay of past conditioning and present-moment arising. This foundational teaching offers crucial insight for understanding how suffering arises and how liberation becomes possible through Right Awareness of these processes.
